Slide this to 0 to restore every Spectre group to its Recommended preset. Experience uses its Default preset. The game applies the reset on its own and then moves the slider back to the current version number.
Any other value does not change your settings.
Example: if potion duration feels wrong after trying several sliders, set this to 0 and leave the menu. The Recommended values come back.

Chooses how enemy levels follow you. Enemies already in the world keep their level: the change applies when they appear again.
None leaves each enemy at its own level. Upscale raises anyone below you up to your level and leaves stronger enemies alone. Match sets every enemy to your level. Soft upscale only lifts enemies who are more than 6 levels below you, up to your level minus 6.
Random rolls between your level plus the lower bound and your level plus the upper bound. At level 32, -4 and +4 roll from 28 to 36. If the upper bound is below the lower one, every enemy is set to your level. Random, no downscaling never rolls below the enemy's own level.
Example: at level 20, Soft upscale turns a level 10 drowner into level 14 and leaves a level 18 one at 18.

On: an enemy above the level delta gains extra per-level bonuses. With the recommended level delta of 10 and ability delta of 5, a level 30 enemy receives about 10 bonuses more than one per level.
Off: each level adds exactly one bonus.
Example: a level 8 wolf is at or below the delta, so it stays on the normal curve either way.

Extra health for monsters. 1 is the recommended bonus. Each whole point above that adds the same bonus again, so 2 is twice the recommended bonus and 4 (the Hardcore preset) is four times.
0 adds no extra health. A negative value reduces health instead.
Example: set this to 0 if drowners and wolves should keep their normal health.

Same scale as the monster health modifier, but only for human enemies. 1 is the recommended bonus, 0 adds nothing, and a negative value reduces their health.
Example: set monsters to 1 and humans to 0 if you want tougher beasts but bandits at their normal health.

Extra damage dealt by enemies. 1 is the recommended bonus, 0 adds none, and a negative value reduces their damage. Bosses add the boss damage slider on top of this.
Example: 0 keeps a drowner's hits at their normal strength; 2 makes ordinary enemies hit about twice as hard as the recommended bonus.

Added on top of the health modifier of that enemy's type. It applies to enemies that hide their health bar, which is how bosses are marked.
Example: with monster health at 1 and this at 2, a normal griffin uses only the monster bonus, while a boss griffin uses both.

On: quests no longer use their recommended level. Experience is not raised or cut according to how far you are from that level, and the quest level lists are not loaded.
Example: finishing a level 30 quest at level 10 pays the base experience, not the reduced amount for being underleveled.

On: quest and combat experience ignore the level gap and pay a fixed amount.
Off: experience grows when the source is above your level and shrinks when it is below, within the game's usual limits.
Example: with it on, a level 5 nekker and a level 25 one of the same kind give the same base experience.

Multiplies quest experience after the other rules. 0 means no change. 1 doubles it, and -0.5 cuts it in half.
Example: a quest that would give 100 experience gives 200 at 1, and 50 at -0.5.

On: tapping the key of a sign starts the cast, after a brief hold of about 0.2 seconds, without keeping the cast button down.
Off: signs use the normal cast button.
Example: with it on, press the Igni key and the sign starts; with it off, you still need the cast button.

On: the boat sinks once your encumbrance passes the percent set on the next slider.
Off: extra weight never sinks it.
Example: with the threshold at 20, crossing 20% over your carry limit while sailing sinks the boat.

On: armor applies its stamina regeneration penalty while your stamina recovers.
Off, which is the recommended value: that penalty is ignored, so heavy armor does not slow recovery.
Example: with it off, a full ursine set does not cut your stamina regeneration.

Adds a flat amount to stamina regeneration during combat. 0 leaves it unchanged. A positive number recovers stamina faster while you fight, and a negative number slows it.
Example: 10 adds that amount on top of your normal regeneration; -10 subtracts the same amount.

Seconds before Whirl or Rend can be used again. The recommended value is 7.5. 0 removes the wait.
Example: at 7.5, after a Whirl you wait 7.5 seconds before the next Whirl or Rend.

On: area loot skips containers you cannot see, such as a chest behind a wall.
Off: distance alone decides, so a container in the next room can be included.
Example: with it on, opening a sack takes the herbs in front of you and ignores a chest on the other side of the house.

Off: area loot skips containers that would count as stealing, such as a merchant's stock.
On: those containers are included too.
Example: with it off, opening your own sack does not pull from the shop chest behind the counter.

On: brewing and distillation advance the clock by the minutes set on the time sliders.
Off: they finish without spending that time.
Example: with 10 minutes per concoction, brewing Swallow moves the clock forward 10 minutes.

On: you can brew without a meditation or an alchemy table.
Off: brewing is limited to those situations, a valid fire, or the alchemy screen.
Example: with it on, you can prepare a potion while exploring a road; with it off, you need to meditate or use a table.

On: primary substance recipes use Spectre's standard ingredient list instead of each recipe's original one. Albedo, Rubedo and Nigredo are left as they are.
Example: with it on, two different primary substances that Spectre treats as the same step ask for the same ingredients.

Seconds that replace a potion's own duration. 0 keeps the potion's duration and allows the added-duration slider to apply.
Any other value replaces the duration, and the added seconds are ignored. The multiplier still applies.
Example: set this to 60 and a Swallow lasts 60 seconds no matter what its formula says.

Extra seconds added to a potion's own duration. This only applies while the duration override is 0. The recommended value is 240, which is 4 minutes.
Example: a potion whose formula lasts 30 seconds lasts 270 seconds with 240 added.

Multiplies the duration after the override and the added seconds. 0 leaves the duration as it is. 2 doubles it.
Example: with the override at 0, 240 seconds added, and this at 2, a 30 second potion becomes (30 + 240) x 2 = 540 seconds.

Seconds a potion spends metabolizing. The recommended value is 30. While it metabolizes, that potion occupies the digestion timer.
Example: at 30, after drinking Swallow you wait 30 seconds before that digestion finishes.

Multiplies potion toxicity. Enhanced potions add 0.5 to the multiplier and superior ones 1.
Example at 1.25, a potion with 20 toxicity: normal 20 x 1.25 = 25, enhanced 20 x 1.75 = 35, superior 20 x 2.25 = 45.
While a potion is in effect, its toxicity falls at this rate. At 1 it is all gone when the potion ends; at 0.24 (recommended), about a quarter. The rest falls later at the residual rate.

Percent chance that a plant spot grows herbs. The recommended value is 30, about one spot in three.
Example: 100 grows herbs on every spot; 30 leaves roughly two out of three spots empty.

How many items one brewing of a recipe produces. The recommended value is 1.
Example: at 1, one brew of Swallow gives one Swallow; at 3, the same brew gives three.

How far past your carry limit the boat sinks, as a percent of that limit. It only matters while Sink Boat If Over Encumbered is on, and only after you are already overencumbered.
The recommended value is 20: more than 20% over the limit sinks the boat. 0 sinks it as soon as you are over the limit. 100 waits until you are carrying twice the limit.
Example: at 20, a load 10% over the limit still floats; a load 25% over sinks.

Lowers the weight of items that count toward your carry limit, as a percent.
0 leaves every item at its normal weight. The recommended value is 20, so those items weigh 20% less. 100 makes them weigh nothing.
Example: a sword of weight 10 weighs 8 at 20, and 5 at 50.

Flat amount added to stamina regeneration while you are out of combat. 0 leaves it unchanged.
This slider only goes down, so it can slow that regeneration or leave it alone; it cannot speed it up. Combat regeneration uses the other slider.
Example: -10 subtracts 10 from the out-of-combat regeneration rate.

Flat amount added to vitality regeneration while you are in combat. 0 leaves it unchanged. It does not change regeneration outside combat.
Example: 5 adds 5 to the combat vitality regeneration rate, so you heal a little faster only while fighting.

Flat amount added to vitality regeneration while you are out of combat. 0 leaves it unchanged. Combat healing uses the other slider.
Example: 10 adds 10 to the out-of-combat vitality regeneration rate.

Changes the stamina cost of sprinting and jumping. The cost is multiplied by 1 plus this number.
0 leaves those costs as they are. 1 doubles them, 0.5 adds half, and -1 removes the cost. Attacks, dodges and signs use the other cost sliders.
Example: a sprint that costs 10 stamina costs 15 at 0.5, and 0 at -1.

Changes the stamina cost of melee actions other than sprinting and jumping: attacks, dodges, rolls, parries and counters. The cost is multiplied by 1 plus this number.
0 leaves those costs as they are. 1 doubles them and -1 removes them. Armor penalties and skill reductions still apply afterwards.
Example: a fast attack that costs 20 stamina costs 10 at -0.5, and 40 at 1.

Changes the stamina cost of casting a sign. The cost is multiplied by 1 plus this number, before armor and skill modifiers.
0 leaves the cost as it is. 1 doubles it and -1 removes it, so later modifiers have nothing left to change. The slider stops at 3, which is four times the cost.
Example: a sign that costs 15 stamina costs 30 at 1, and 0 at -1.

Extra seconds before stamina starts regenerating after you spend it. 0 leaves the pause as it is.
A positive number makes you wait longer. A negative number shortens the pause, but it never goes below 0 seconds.
Example: if the pause is 1 second, 1 makes it 2 seconds, and -1 makes it 0.

Seconds you must wait before casting the same sign again after a normal cast.
The recommended value is 5. 0 removes the wait. Alternate sign mode uses the other slider.
Example: at 5, after casting Igni you wait 5 seconds before Igni is ready again. Aard, Quen, Yrden and Axii each keep their own wait.

Seconds you must wait before using that sign's alternate mode again.
The recommended value is 7.5. 0 removes the wait. A normal cast uses the sign cooldown slider instead.
Example: at 7.5, after holding Igni for the fire stream you wait 7.5 seconds before that alternate cast is ready again.
